_comment: Every command below shares one interpreter probe, `_pyexe`. It RUNS each
candidate before accepting it, rather than trusting the first name that
resolves.
The previous form was `command -v python3 || command -v py || command -v
python`, and on Windows that is actively wrong: `python3` commonly resolves
to the Store alias stub in WindowsApps, which exists and is executable, so
`command -v` SUCCEEDS and the `||` fallbacks never fire. Every dispatched
hook was then invoked through an interpreter that cannot run it — the hook
exited non-zero without producing output, and because a PreToolUse hook
that fails to run is indistinguishable from one that ran and allowed, the
entire guard set silently did nothing. Reproduced by putting a
non-functional `python3` first on PATH: current probe picks it and the hook
exits 9009 with no warning; this probe skips it.
THE THREE NAMES ARE NOT ENOUGH ON THIS MACHINE, and the candidate list now
ends with two Windows install globs. Measured, not assumed: the hook's PATH
and the PATH a Bash tool call sees are DIFFERENT, and the real interpreter
is on the second but not the first. Under a captured hook PATH, `python3`
resolves to ~/.local/bin/python3 -- a wrapper delegating to `python`, which
there is the Store alias stub -- `py` is absent, and `python` is the same
stub. All three fail the version assertion, so the probe correctly reported
that nothing was usable and every dispatched hook stopped running.
This is why `test_probe_selects_something` can pass while the hooks are
dead: it runs the probe under the TEST process's PATH, which has the real
python on it. A probe that selects an interpreter in pytest proves nothing
about the interpreter a hook gets. The only evidence that counts is a
harmless command sent through the tool that MUST be denied, watched being
denied, in a live session.
An unmatched glob stays literal, `command -v` then fails, and the loop
continues -- so the two Windows paths are inert on macOS, where `python3`
resolves on the first candidate anyway. `$c` is quoted in `command -v`
because the expanded paths are no longer bare names.
`CLA_PY_SEARCH` exists so the REFUSAL PATH stays testable. The two probe
tests poison PATH and assert the probe finds nothing; a fallback rooted at
$HOME defeats that, and clearing the env does not help because bash supplies
HOME from the passwd entry when it is absent. The braces use `-` and not
`:-` deliberately, so setting it EMPTY suppresses the fallback while leaving
it unset keeps the default. It is not a security boundary: the version
assertion still applies to whatever it names, and anyone who can set the
environment can already do worse.
These wirings assert the interpreter's VERSION via stdout, not merely its
liveness: a bare `-c "import sys"` passes on Python 2.7 and on any wrapper
that swallows `-c` and exits 0. The candidate ORDER is the other
load-bearing half, and `python3` must stay first.
This block used to describe the probe by comparing it with the `claw`
launcher's. `claw` has been deleted — it existed only to dodge
`guard-worktree-isolation.py`'s SessionStart heartbeat, and that hook is
gone too — so hooks.json is now the sole holder of this probe, and
`test_every_wiring_probes_the_same_candidates_in_the_same_order` pins it.
Note also that JSON has no substitution: `_pyexe` is a reference copy, and
`test_every_wiring_shares_one_probe` is what holds the inlined copies equal
to it.
Failure is announced rather than silent: if NO candidate runs, the command
says so on stderr and exits 1. NON-ZERO is deliberate, and this block used
to say 'exits 0 (fail-open)' — describing, as intended behaviour, exactly
the invisible degradation the probe exists to prevent. stderr from an
exit-0 hook reaches the debug log only, so a machine with no usable Python
would have looked protected while running no guards at all.
`test_every_wiring_exits_non_zero_when_no_interpreter_works` pins the 1;
the code and the test were fixed once already and this comment was not,
which matters because it is the sentence a future editor consults before
changing that exit code.
_pyexe: PYEXE=; for c in python3 py python ${CLA_PY_SEARCH-$HOME/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python3*/python.exe /c/Python3*/python.exe}; do p=$(command -v "$c" 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ "$("$p" -c "import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3,8) else 0)" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && PYEXE=$p && break; done; if [ -z "${PYEXE:-}" ]; then echo "cla: no working python interpreter (tried python3, py, python) — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; fi;

hooks.command: PYEXE=; for c in python3 py python ${CLA_PY_SEARCH-$HOME/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python3*/python.exe /c/Python3*/python.exe}; do p=$(command -v "$c" 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ "$("$p" -c "import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3,8) else 0)" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && PYEXE=$p && break; done; if [ -z "${PYEXE:-}" ]; then echo "cla: no working python interpreter (tried python3, py, python) — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; fi; "$PYEXE" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/dispatch-edit-write-pretooluse.py"
